description: CodeQL policy baseline. The ceiling is a RATCHET, not a budget: it records how many open findings the tree carried when it was last measured, so a new one fails and a fixed one is visible as slack to lock in.
establishedBy: RootLco CodeQL Application Remediation and Security Hardening, from the SARIF of the hosted `code-security` job on the remediation branch.
expectedLanguagesNote: A language that was not analysed cannot be reported clean. If a SARIF for either is missing the gate fails rather than judging the languages it happens to have — the AR-45 shape, where a scan that enumerated nothing read as a scan that found nothing.
maximumOpenFindingsNote: Zero OPEN findings — where open means neither dismissed by GitHub nor covered by an approved dismissal below. Every alert in the 21-alert baseline was fixed: the two application findings structurally, the fifteen script findings directly, the four vacuous assertions repaired. A ceiling above zero would be a budget for the next one. The count deliberately includes medium and low, which is how the one dismissal below was caught at all — GitHub's own CodeQL check reported that run as SUCCESS, because it blocks only on high and critical.

dismissals.source: The JSON body of an authenticated `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/check-runs` response from api.github.com over TLS. It is not attacker-controlled in any reachable sense: the request is made by a maintainer, with that maintainer's own token, against this repository, and the only fields read are `name`, `status`, `conclusion`, `app.slug`, `output.title` and `html_url`. A party able to forge that response already controls the repository the gate is protecting.
dismissals.sink: `writeFileSync` to a path the OPERATOR names on the command line via `--json`, in an ephemeral working directory. The path is never derived from the response. Nothing consumes the file automatically — it is evidence a human attaches to a gate record.
dismissals.reason: CodeQL tracks HTTP-response data reaching a filesystem write and does not model `safeText` as a sanitiser, so the flow persists no matter how the content is cleaned. The content IS cleaned: every field passes through `safeText`, which strips C0/C1 control characters, escapes backslashes and then pipes, and caps length. Verified by reproduction — the hostile input `evil\|name` yields exactly one Markdown table cell, so it cannot break out of the cell it is rendered into. What remains is the flow itself, which is the script's entire purpose: a report about an API response necessarily contains data from that API response. Dismissed as a false positive in impact, not in existence.
dismissals.expiryRationale: Two quarters. Long enough that it is not busywork, short enough that it cannot become permanent without somebody looking at `safeText` and this justification again.

dismissalsNote: ONE entry, and it is in a script this initiative wrote — which is uncomfortable and is the reason it carries a full reproduction rather than an assertion. Every other alert in the 21-alert baseline was FIXED; none of the pre-existing ones was waived. A dismissal must name the exact rule, the exact path, a reproduction of why the source cannot be attacker-controlled AND why the sink is safe, a reviewer, a review date and an expiry. An entry matching nothing fails the gate; the same rule at a different path is a new finding, not a covered one; and nothing under src/ may be dismissed here at all.

dismissalSchema.ruleId: the exact CodeQL rule, e.g. js/incomplete-sanitization
dismissalSchema.path: the exact repo-relative path — dismissals are per-path on purpose
dismissalSchema.source: what the dataflow source is, and why it cannot be attacker-controlled
dismissalSchema.sink: what the sink is, and why reaching it is safe
dismissalSchema.reason: the refutation, reproducible by someone else
dismissalSchema.expiresOn: ISO date; an expired dismissal fails the gate

applicationScopeNote: Findings under src/ are APPLICATION findings and may never be dismissed by this file at all — they are fixed or refuted in code. The split is enforced by codeql-policy.mjs, which fails if a dismissal covers an application path.
